_about: A small, hand-checked list of well-known addresses. Each entry was checked against public explorer labels and incident reports. Arc entries come from the official Arc contract address page. It is a starting point, not a full blocklist; GoPlus covers far more addresses. 'chains' lists where the label applies, or ['*'] for every chain.

addresses.name: Tornado Cash: Router
addresses.note: A mixer hides where funds came from. Tornado Cash was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and delisted in 2025, but links to it are still a common money-laundering signal.

addresses.name: Ronin Bridge Exploiter
addresses.note: Used in the 2022 Ronin bridge hack. On the US OFAC sanctions list.

addresses.name: Bybit Exploiter 1
addresses.note: First address to receive funds stolen from Bybit in February 2025.

addresses.name: Euler Finance Exploiter 2
addresses.note: Used in the March 2023 Euler Finance flash-loan attack. Most funds were later returned.

addresses.name: Wormhole Network Exploiter
addresses.note: Received funds from the February 2022 Wormhole bridge hack.

addresses.name: Null address
addresses.note: Tokens sent here can never be moved. Often used to burn tokens or LP tokens.

addresses.name: Dead address
addresses.note: A common burn address. Nobody holds its key.

addresses.name: USDC mint or burn (Arc)
addresses.note: On Arc, new USDC (for example USDC bridged in with Circle's CCTP) arrives as a transfer from the zero address, and burned USDC goes to it. Plain sends to it are rejected.

addresses.name: USDC (Arc ERC-20 interface)
addresses.note: The ERC-20 view of Arc's native USDC. Same balance, shown with 6 decimals instead of 18. Listed on https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/contract-addresses
